extracted.intended_audience: Authors and peer reviewers submitting to or reviewing for JEED (journal)
extracted.subtask_short: JEED AI policy for authors and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-level formal policy describing allowed and prohibited uses of generative AI and related tools by authors preparing submissions and by reviewers during peer review, including disclosure, citation, recordkeeping, and confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI tools cannot be listed as authors
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools, such as ChatGPT, cannot be listed as authors on papers as they are non-legal entities and cannot take responsibility for the published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE authorship and AI policy; only human authors who can take responsibility and be held accountable may be credited as authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent disclosure of AI tool use by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use AI tools to assist in writing the manuscript, producing images or graphical elements, coding, or in collecting and analyzing data as long as authors are fully transparent about this use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full description of which AI tools were used, and how, should be included in the Materials and Methods section or the Acknowledgments section, or a separate AI Disclosure Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must verify and take responsibility for AI-generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: All content generated by an AI tool should be carefully checked by the authors for accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are fully responsible for the content of their manuscript, including sections created by AI tools, and are therefore liable for any breach of publication ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for each AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use AI tools in the preparation of your JEED submission, record this information for each use of AI and keep it for your records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record: tool name and version; general reason for use of the tool; name(s) of author(s) generating query; date and time of query; query and response wording; any additional relevant information. Consider following MIT Libraries suggestions for saving AI-generated output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review AI tool terms and conditions before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the terms and conditions of any AI tool before using it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure understanding of data use, privacy, and intellectual property implications prior to using the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite AI tool use in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Include citation information whenever you have used AI tools to gather information, write text, edit text, synthesize ideas, find connections, or clean and manipulate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite AI tools parenthetically within the text, in CSE Name–Year Style, as personal communication. Do not include an end reference. Instead, include full descriptions of AI tool use in the Materials and Methods section or the Acknowledgments section, or in a separate AI Disclosure Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation/reference managers and built-in proofreaders excluded from AI-tool definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation/reference managers, such as Zotero, EndNote, and Mendeley, and built-in proofreading or grammar assistants are not considered AI tools under this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tools can be used without the AI disclosure requirements described for generative AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not upload manuscript content to public generative AI tools (reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploading manuscript files or text (including reference lists), images, supplementary materials, or digital communication, from or related to any manuscript under review, to a public gen AI tool or LLM is expressly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action violates the confidentiality of peer review and the author’s copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using public gen AI tools for review report drafting or verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Using public gen AI tools to improve one’s own or others’ writing outputs, organize peer review reports, or verify references is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risks include public exposure of confidential research information and introduction of potentially inaccurate information into the written record. Closed or enterprise AI tools that protect data inside an institution or organization may be used for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable reviewer searches with public gen AI and web engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Using public gen AI tools and web search engines for general, topic-related searches is allowable under this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses are limited to general background/topic searches that do not involve uploading confidential manuscript content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable use of citation/reference managers and proofreading assistants for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Using citation/reference managers (such as Zotero, EndNote, and Mendeley) and built-in proofreading or grammar assistants is allowable under this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools are not treated as generative AI for the purposes of prohibitions on uploading confidential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact AE for exceptions or guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer identifies a need to use an AI tool for a situation not detailed here, they may contact their AE for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JEED will revisit the policy regularly and make adjustments as AI technology evolves; use the AE as the channel for case-by-case decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to COPE authorship and AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: JEED follows the authorship and Artificial Intelligence (AI) policy of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should align with COPE guidance (COPE position statements on AI and authorship) in addition to these JEED-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider linking/saving AI-generated outputs for transparency and replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Also consider linking to your AI-generated output within your paper by following suggestions from the MIT Libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saving AI content (queries and outputs) supports transparency and reproducibility; follow MIT Libraries guidance on how to save and cite AI-generated content.
